speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Miss Chan, Mr Louis Ng and Ms Poh Li San asked how the Government is supporting SMEs to implement green measures in the supply chain.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The Government is providing local enterprises with more tools and resources to become sustainable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Companies can tap on capability-building programmes, such as courses and playbooks on decarbonisation, or funding support to do sustainability reporting and invest in energy-efficient equipment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This better prices the externality of carbon emissions, and nudges businesses and individuals to reduce their carbon footprint.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Enhancing energy efficiency will help businesses cut energy costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Ms Poh would be happy to know that NEA's E2F has been supporting SMEs in the manufacturing sector since 2017.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Enhancements to the E2F from 2022 onwards, such as increasing the grant support cap from 50% to 70%, has increased take-up rate by four-fold to 48 projects.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The amount of committed funding also increased from around $700,000 to around $2.1 million post-enhancement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The expanded EEG will benefit more sectors, including construction, maritime and the data centres industry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: It will adopt a two-tier structure, with higher support of up to 70% provided to companies that wish to make larger investments to drive greater energy efficiency.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The Government will continue to work closely with the industry, including TACs, to proactively reach out to SMEs to promote awareness of the EEG.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Adopting energy-efficient equipment will translate to significant cost savings for businesses and households.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: NEA’s energy efficiency labels and standards have helped companies and consumers make informed decisions since 2008.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: For instance, the average energy efficiency of air-conditioners and refrigerators improved by 59% and 42% respectively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This is equivalent to the annual energy consumption of about 405,000 4-room housing units and translates to annual overall household energy savings of more than $500 million.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Water heaters are the third-highest energy consuming household appliance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: There are more energy-efficient options, such as instantaneous water heaters, which on average consume about 50% less electricity than electric storage water heaters.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This enables homeowners to save on energy bills.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Commercial storage refrigerators are prevalent in food and beverage establishments, like hawker centres, food courts and restaurants, and can account for about one-third of hawkers' electricity usage.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: As refrigerators consume energy throughout the day, we encourage businesses to purchase energy-efficient models to enjoy long-term savings, such as inverter technology refrigerators that are on average 40% more energy-efficient.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This will result in annual energy cost savings of about $700, with payback on capital expenditure within a year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Overall, the lifecycle cost of such efficient models are up to 60% lower than that of standard models.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Furthermore, businesses can apply for the EEG to offset up to 70% of the upfront costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: In 2019, to optimise energy consumption at the systems-level, we introduced Minimum Energy Efficiency Standards (MEES) for water-cooled chilled water systems to encourage adoption of energy-efficient chilled water operations by industrial facilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Mandatory MEES requirements were introduced for new industrial facilities in 2020.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Besides improving energy efficiency, pursuing sustainable waste management practices should also be a priority for organisations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: By following the "3Rs" to reduce, reuse and recycle waste, businesses can increase efficiency and lower costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Ms Poh asked how we are supporting businesses in building up capabilities to better manage their waste.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Businesses have suggested that it would be useful to appoint staff with formal training to champion the shift towards circular and zero-waste business models.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: In response, NEA has worked with training providers to introduce Zero Waste Manager (ZWM) courses to train participants to implement "3R" efforts and integrate them into their companies' organisational culture.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The courses will also guide companies in fulfilling regulatory requirements, such as Mandatory Waste Reporting (MWR).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Not only will the courses benefit some 750 companies covered under the MWR scheme, they can also equip other companies with the necessary knowledge to kickstart their waste reduction and recycling journeys.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Additionally, the ZWM course will benefit employees and companies in the waste management sector looking to provide value-added services, such as waste consultancy and audit services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We encourage all companies to appoint and train staff to lead their waste management and "3R" efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: These two- to three- day courses are developed and conducted in partnership with three training providers, the Waste Management and Recycling Association of Singapore, Republic Polytechnic and NTUC Learning Hub.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: To ensure these courses are accessible and affordable, they will be subsidised by SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG) and whitelisted under Workforce Singapore's (WSG) Career Conversion Programmes (CCPs) for Sustainability Professionals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Mr Gan and Ms Hany Soh asked if there will be support for households which will face higher utility bills from the carbon tax increase.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We remain committed to helping households cope with cost of living.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: As announced by Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong, additional U-Save rebates will be disbursed to HDB households as part of the enhanced Assurance Package, cushioning increases in utility bills.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will enhance support for households wishing to be more energy- and water-efficient, which will also help lower their utility bills.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Launched in 2020, the existing Climate Friendly Households Programme (CFHP) provides $225 worth of vouchers to 1- to 3-room HDB households, consisting of a $150 refrigerator voucher, $50 shower fittings voucher and $25 LED lighting voucher.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: As of January 2024, more than 141,000 households have registered for their Climate Vouchers and about 54,000 vouchers have been utilised.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: To give households more time to utilise their current set of Climate Vouchers, we have extended the qualifying redemption period to 20 March 2024.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Mr Ng asked if we will be expanding the programme to include more households and appliances.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This is to encourage wider adoption of energy- and water-efficient products.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: To Mr Gan's and Mr Ng's queries, other additions, like direct current fans, will help households keep cool in a more energy-efficient manner.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The 10 eligible products contribute to around 60% of an average household's electricity consumption and around 90% of water consumption.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: To make it more convenient for households to use the Climate Vouchers, more retailers will come onboard the programme, taking the total number of participating retailers to 14, with about 300 stores islandwide.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: With these enhancements, we hope to incentivise more households to choose resource-efficient options from the outset or when their appliances and fittings are due for replacement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: HDB households who have used the $225 vouchers under the current CFHP can also claim the new $300 vouchers under the enhanced CFHP following its commencement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Unlike the current CFHP where the voucher amount is fixed for each eligible product type, the enhanced CFHP will allow households to have more flexibility in using their vouchers and select different denominations when purchasing eligible appliances.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Members of the public who need support in claiming the Climate Vouchers online may call NEA's hotline for assistance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: (In Mandarin):   NEA will enhance the Climate Friendly Households Programme to encourage more households to adopt more environmentally friendly and sustainable lifestyles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: In the long run, using more energy-efficient and water-saving appliances and fittings can help households save on utility expenses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Through the enhanced programme, more households will benefit.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The total amount of vouchers and the variety of eligible electrical appliances and fittings will also increase.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: All HDB households will receive $300 worth of Climate Vouchers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: They can use the vouchers to purchase 10 types of energy-efficient and water-saving appliances and fittings, including direct current fans and washing machines, from participating retailers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Starting from 15 April 2024, one member of each household can go to redeem.gov.sg to claim the vouchers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Elderly residents and those who face difficulties with Internet access can seek assistance via NEA's hotline. : Reducing waste will also reduce emissions and cut costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We should thus seek to reduce wasteful consumption, which Ms Carrie Tan has spoken about.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Sustainable consumption involves the responsible management of packaging and products at their end-of-life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This is a significant increase from the 9,000 tonnes collected as of December 2022.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Overall, collection rates have improved, thanks to the close collaboration with ALBA, retailers and Town Councils to publicise the scheme and encourage participation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: However, we must continue to double down on efforts to achieve our target collection rates of 60% of large household appliances and 20% of other regulated consumer products' put-to-market weight.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Collection rates for lamps and household batteries have tripled to 4% and 10% respectively whilst the collection rate for ICT equipment increased slightly to 5%.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: However, the collection rate for large household appliances has declined from 18% to 15%.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: To improve this, we will strengthen collaboration with retailers to further publicise their obligatory one-for-one takeback services to customers and continue to work with Town Councils through the quarterly collection drives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We seek everyone's continued support to deposit their e-waste via the various channels available.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Last year, we amended the Resource Sustainability Act to put in place the legislative framework for the Beverage Container Return Scheme (BCRS).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We are working with stakeholders on scheme implementation and will share more details when ready.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Beyond BCRS, we are exploring other initiatives to manage packaging waste.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: In 2021, we implemented the Mandatory Packaging Reporting scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This raises awareness amongst companies on the amount of packaging they generate and spurs them to reduce packaging use.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Building on our current initiatives, we are exploring the feasibility of expanding the EPR approach to broader packaging waste types.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We have awarded a consultancy study to review overseas best practices and recommend a suitable scheme for Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will consult stakeholders at an appropriate juncture.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This study is expected to be completed by 2025.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Chairman, to reach net-zero, everyone must pitch in.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The Government will play its part in greening the Public Service and supporting businesses and households to contribute.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Let us all embrace going green, which is not just environmentally friendly, but certainly can also be wallet friendly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Chairman, the effects of climate change are already upon us.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I will speak on our approach in enhancing coastal protection and food security.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Ms Nadia Samdin and Ms Poh Li San asked how the V3 study will be used.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will progressively share V3 data with regional and local partners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will also incorporate V3 data into our research, such as the Climate Impact Science Research and the work of the Coastal Protection and Flood Resilience Institute (CFI) Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We have begun preparations for coastal protection with site-specific studies of Singapore's coastlines since 2021.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Louis Chua, Ms Nadia Samdin and Ms Poh Li San asked about the progress of the Lim Chu Kang Master Plan (LCKMP).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The comprehensive master planning effort is now underway.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We aim to harness synergies between land and sea farms in the Western Johor Strait so that farms can grow with greater resource efficiency.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The detailed plan will optimise land use and put in place the necessary transport infrastructure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: To Mr Louis Chua's suggestion that clustering will not give economies of scale and decentralisation is better, I would like to share that the key feedback from our engagement with stakeholders, including farmers and industry players, since 2021, is that it will not be commercially viable nor an effective use of space and resources if farms were to build individual smaller-scale infrastructure for their own needs alone.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Following his suggestion would mean that we are back to status quo and would miss the opportunity for Lim Chu Kang Master Plan to create better efficiencies and new opportunities to take our agri-food sector to a new high level.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We are, in fact, studying the viability of shared facilities, such as centralised processing facilities, for better economies of scale.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We are also exploring innovative solutions that could intensify land use while guarding against sea level rise, such as growing in a "stacked farm approach".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Farms affected by the redevelopment have been given time to transit and can bid in land tenders launched by SFA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The Public Utilities Board (PUB) will be extending Our Coastal Conversation in the first half of 2025 to discuss the possibilities for the north-west coast and this will include development plans for the Lim Chu Kang Master Plan.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This would delineate the roles and responsibilities of various stakeholders, safeguard land for coastal protection measures and future upgrades to cater for uncertainties in climate projections, and regulate and enforce against activities that could pose a risk to coastal protection measures and ensure that PUB's coastal protection standards are met.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We intend to kickstart consultations with stakeholders later this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Concurrently, PUB has started on a two-year study, from November 2023, to develop a new Code of Practice.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This will guide and standardise the design, implementation as well as the operation and maintenance of coastal protection measures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As we import more than 90% of our food, Singapore is particularly vulnerable to global food supply chain disruptions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Recent examples include disease outbreaks, policy decisions by foreign governments and, of course, geopolitical tensions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: To Ms Nadia Samdin's and Ms Poh Li San's questions on ensuring food resilience, import source diversification will remain the cornerstone of our food security strategy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will continue to facilitate food imports from new sources by working closely with industry and governments globally.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For example, we approved the export of eggs and live chickens from Indonesia to Singapore in April and May 2023 respectively, and Türkiye for eggs in September 2023.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: SFA also works closely with industry players to put in place robust business continuity plans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Ms Poh Li San asked about the progress of our "30 by 30" vision and support for the agri-food industry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This goal is very ambitious but it signifies our determination to make progress.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: It has not been easy for our farms, especially due to developmental delays during the COVID-19 pandemic and strong headwinds due to inflationary pressures and higher costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Global agri-tech companies have also not been spared from the near-term investment headwinds.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Even as we deal with these challenges, we will still forge ahead to strengthen our food supply resilience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: To help our farms cope with the higher energy costs, SFA, in April last year, enhanced the Agri-Food Cluster Transformation (ACT) Fund and introduced the Energy Efficiency Programme (EEP), providing farms with co-funding to adopt energy-efficient technologies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will also continue to upskill and build the pipeline of agri-workforce to meet the sector's needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Ms Nadia Samdin and Ms Poh Li San asked about the progress of the Singapore Aquaculture Plan (SAP).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We have been working with agencies to increase and optimise aquaculture spaces to encourage better farming practices and invest in R&D through our AquaPolis programme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Optimising our limited sea spaces for aquaculture will require us to balance competing priorities, including maritime activities and biodiversity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: How can we come to a consensus on the right balance to strike?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: How can we achieve win-win outcomes to help Singapore responsibly manage our sea space for our present and future needs while preserving biodiversity?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In October 2023, we brought together key stakeholders from industry, academia, nature groups and Government agencies to envision the answers to these key questions and to guide the development of productive and sustainable aquaculture for Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We are midway into our discussion, but we have started to converge on some key principles to develop the sector in a manner that is suited for our local context.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: First, we will support industry to scale up through enabling regulation, technology and infrastructure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Agencies will proactively review legislation and regulations to guide resilient and sustainable aquaculture production.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Before new sites are tendered, SFA works with agencies to conduct environmental studies to assess the potential impact of aquaculture developments and identify proper mitigating measures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will help farmers to adopt more sustainable farming practices and technologies, including closed containment aquaculture systems.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will also facilitate the necessary supporting infrastructure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Second, we will consider competing sea space uses and ecological sensitivity upfront when identifying aquaculture sites.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Third, we will be outcome-based and science-based in ensuring sustainable production.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Farming need not be at the expense of the health of our waters.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Ultimately, for the agri-tech sector and the agri-food sector to thrive, our farmers will need sufficient consumer demand to be commercially viable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Some farms are, in fact, ready to ramp up production, but our farmers need to know that it will be met with a corresponding increase in demand.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As consumers, we all have a part to play in strengthening Singapore's Food Story.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Last year, as part of the Forward SG exercise, we launched the AfA that brought together various industry stakeholders to encourage increased offtake of local produce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: SAFEF will partner traders and food processing companies via longer-term commercial aggregator contracts to better match supply and demand.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This gives certainty to both producers and buyers and also allows better price negotiations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For example, SAFEF aggregated locally farmed marine tilapia from several fish farmers at the Western Johor Strait and marketed it as “The Straits Fish”.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: With additional support from Hai Sia Seafood, a food processing and distributor company, as well as Chang Cheng Group, a food services company, “The Straits Fish” dishes were officially launched on 17 February 2024 across the Group's "zi char" chain, Ming Kitchen Seafood.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Initially, they were uncertain about how consumers would respond, so the partnership commenced with a modest launch of 200 kilogrammes of fish.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The dishes were well received and sold out within the day.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: SAFEF, Hai Sia Seafood as well as retailers, such as FairPrice supermarket, are also intending to pilot dedicated retail shelves for local produce by the second half of this year, so it will be easier for consumers to purchase and support local produce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The AfA also supported the Farm-to-Table Recognition Programme (FTTRP), launched in March last year, which recognises food businesses that procure locally produced ingredients.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: To Ms Nadia Samdin’s question, I am pleased to share that there are 50 businesses onboard to date.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: SFA plans to onboard at least a total of 100 food establishments over the next year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The Government has also taken the lead to support the FTTRP.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Since October 2023, Government procurement has incorporated a weighted criterion for sustainability into our catering contract.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This allows FTTRP-recognised food caterers, which uses sustainably sourced local produce, to receive additional points that increase their chances of securing Government catering contracts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I believe that more caterers will start using local produce if more Singaporeans, businesses and community groups support our local farms by asking for catering to use local ingredients and local produce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: At today’s tea break, Members would have sampled an array of local dishes using locally sourced food ingredients.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: From the savoury delights of Nyonya laksa prepared from local prawn, eggs and beansprouts, to tandoori fish made with our local harvest, and sweets, such as peach croissant with basil cream, made with locally farmed basil.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Ms Nadia Samdin also asked about the SG Fresh Produce (SGFP) logo and if wet market stallholders that supply local produce could be better recognised.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: SFA has also developed marketing materials featuring the SGFP logo for wet market stallholders to help generate higher sales.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: SFA will also work with partners, like the Singapore Chefs’ Association, on programmes, such as cooking classes, to promote SGFP and the FTTRP.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Ms Poh Li San asked how the public can do their part to support Singapore’s food resiliency.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Consumers like you and I must recognise our vulnerability to food supply disruptions and be flexible in our food choices in the event of a disruption.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Hence, as part of Total Defence 40th Anniversary, SFA in collaboration with MOE and SATS, conducted a pilot Food Resilience Preparedness Project (FRPP) involving an estimated 50,000 students from 40 secondary schools.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This involved the distribution of retort meal packs made with locally sourced ingredients and educated students on the importance of food security, the benefits of local produce and how we can all jointly strengthen Singapore’s food supply resilience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Since August last year, SFA has been engaging with industry associations and key stakeholders on the proposed enhancements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Relevant feedback has been incorporated into the draft Bill.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: NEA provides a conducive environment for hawkers to operate, enabling them to strike a balance between pricing their food affordably and sustaining their livelihood.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: NEA lets out hawker stalls through monthly tender exercises, which are transparent and fair.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: There is no minimum bid and subletting is not allowed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Individuals can bid for a stall at a monthly rental as low as $1, while others may choose to submit higher bids to secure stalls at popular locations, as they factor in considerations such as footfall and expected patronage.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Some popular hawker centres, such as Newton Food Centre, attract additional clientele, such as tourists, and enjoy better footfall over longer business hours.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Rent will be adjusted towards the assessed market rent after the first three years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In fact, only about 4% of cooked food stalls in hawker centres today are paying rent at above the assessed market rent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: These stalls would be in their initial three years of tenancy, and their rental would be based on their tender bid.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: When they renew their tenancy at the end of the three years, it will be adjusted to the assessed market rent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For Socially-conscious Enterprise Hawker Centres (SEHCs), NEA will consider proposals from prospective operators with lower rental and operating costs to hawkers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Operators are not allowed to vary the charges to hawkers over the term of tenancy and they are to stagger stall rental prices for the first three years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: To help hawkers enhance their operations and productivity, NEA has also implemented measures, such as the Productive Hawker Centre (PHC) programme and Hawkers’ Productivity Grant (HPG).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: On hawker food affordability, NEA does not regulate hawker food prices to avoid distorting the true cost of hawker food.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Our hawkers should be given the autonomy to price their food based on multiple considerations, such as operating costs and market conditions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Edward Chia asked if the Ministry had conducted a survey on hawkers’ average earnings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: While we do not collect this data from hawkers, NEA does conduct regular surveys on hawker food prices and their cost components and will continue to ensure a conducive business environment for our hawkers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Today, patrons can continue to find affordable options in all hawker centres, including at the SEHCs, where operators have committed that all stalls will provide at least one budget meal option.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The public can also utilise Community Development Council (CDC) Vouchers provided under the Assurance Package at hawker centres and coffee shops.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh would be glad to know that NEA has implemented various programmes to encourage aspiring hawkers to enter the trade.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: NEA's Hawkers' Development Programme and Incubation Stall Programme provide holistic training to equip aspiring hawkers with skills needed to run a successful hawker business.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Over 60 hawkers have joined the trade through these programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: NEA will also continue to build new hawker centres to ensure that Singaporeans will continue to have access to affordable and tasty hawker food.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I am pleased to share that three new SEHC hawker centres will be opening this year, namely Woodleigh Village, Anchorvale Village and Punggol Coast Hawker Centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Chairman, as a small nation constrained by land and resources, the road ahead to strengthen our coastal resilience and food security may seem challenging and daunting, but it is a path that we will navigate together, to transform our limitations into opportunities for growth.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Through our collective efforts, we will pave the way for a thriving and secure future for generations to come.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Chairman, creating a Clean, Green and Resilient Shared Future for Singapore is a collective effort.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: During our Forward SG engagements, Singaporeans acknowledged that the whole society needs to work together to ensure that Singapore remains a clean, green and safe home.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Our education efforts and campaigns over the years have paid off and Singaporeans are generally civic-minded.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: However, we continue to observe some persistent issues that require us to go beyond just public education.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Public hygiene remains a top priority for MSE.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Ms Rahayu Mahzam, Mr Liang Eng Hwa and Mr Murali Pillai have asked about MSE’s efforts to enhance cleanliness.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This year, we will be working more closely with the community and ramping up our efforts to address persistent pain points, such as littering hotspots and dirty public toilets.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The pandemic may be over, but Singapore needs a clean environment to be well-prepared to tackle future public health threats.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Based on our cleanliness surveys, many still believe that the responsibility to keep Singapore clean lies with the Government and our “army of cleaners”.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Our cleaners are already busy cleaning up natural litter, such as fallen leaves, and accidental litter, such as spillages.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Let us not add to their heavy workload with intentional litter by leaving or throwing our litter for them to clean up after us.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To tackle ongoing and persistent issues, we adopt a multi-pronged approach.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Legislation and enforcement are critical to help us tackle the inconsiderate behaviour of a small number of people who are not as socially responsible and to shape social norms for the wider population.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Ms Nadia Samdin asked about the Tray Return Initiative.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This was launched in 2013 to encourage diners to return their trays after their meals.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: However, the Tray and Crockery Return Rate remained low despite public education efforts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To Ms Nadia’s query, tray return is a key measure that helps tackle bird nuisance issues at hawker centres.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NEA currently works with stakeholders, such as Hawkers’ Associations and cleaning contractors, to clear used crockery promptly and implement proper food waste management.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NEA, together with the Town Councils, has also implemented anti-bird measures, such as netting at tray return racks.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Bird control efforts are also carried out where necessary.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To Mr Gan Thiam Poh’s query, we similarly use both public education and enforcement to curb high-rise littering.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: While we continue to educate the public on the dangers of high-rise littering, offenders, including first timers, are sent to Court and receive stiffer financial penalties and Corrective Work Orders (CWOs).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In July 2023, we introduced the statutory presumption provision for littering from residential flats to hold the registered owners or tenants responsible.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We also encourage residents to follow guidelines by HDB or Town Councils on proper placement of objects in open spaces.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Any cases of potential killer litter will be referred to the Police for investigation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The number of feedback on ground littering from 2022 to 2023 has increased about 15%, compared to the two years before the pandemic.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To tackle littering hotspots, we will adopt a more targeted approach.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: These blitzes will be more visible by deploying uniformed officers to patrol these hotspots and putting up standees on the number of enforcement actions taken.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will also deploy non-uniformed officers to catch litterbugs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Recalcitrant littering offenders will carry out CWO at high footfall areas, like transport nodes, town centres and city locations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: An average of around 500 CWOs are issued to offenders each year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: They wear pink and yellow vests that clearly state "Corrective Work Order" while picking up litter.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This will improve NEA’s remote surveillance capabilities, facilitate efficient deployment of resources by enabling investigations into public hygiene offences, as well as deter would-be offenders.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: However, even if someone is caught on camera, we are unable to follow up with enforcement action if we cannot identify the person.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NEA will work with community stakeholders to identify these offenders.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: If there are still no leads, NEA will explore putting up images of these offenders at the places where they had littered to seek the wider community’s assistance in identifying them.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We hope that this will invoke collective community ownership to keep the common spaces clean and also deter potential litterbugs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Public toilets remain a bugbear of many Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We have stepped up our enforcement efforts on unhygienic public toilets, including at food establishments.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Since April 2020, first time offenders who fail to keep public toilets in their premises clean and in good working condition, are fined up to $400 instead of getting a warning letter.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Implicated retail food businesses would also incur demerit points, and some have resulted in the suspension of licences.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: So, I agree with Ms Poh Li San and Ms Rahayu Mahzam that users and the community need to be involved as well.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Andrew Khng, Chairman of the Public Hygiene Council (PHC), and I will co-chair this taskforce.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The taskforce will tap on the expertise of public sector agencies, Town Councils, premises managers, academia and trade and industry associations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The focus will be on toilets that consistently fare poorly in cleanliness surveys, such as those at coffeeshops and hawker centres.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will incorporate new technology to improve the efficiency of our cleaning and vector control operations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NEA will share relevant footage and data with premises operators so that they can conduct targeted interventions to eliminate potential rat nesting grounds.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Second, we will explore the use of AI-powered video analytics to supplement performance audits of contracted cleaning companies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This will be productive than manual inspections in detecting cleaning lapses.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Many Singaporeans we engaged during the Forward SG conversations agreed that we cannot just rely on cleaners and cleaning technology to keep Singapore clean.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Hence, MSE will further strengthen our partnerships with the community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The PHC will launch the latest edition of the "Keep Singapore Clean" campaign next month to galvanise Singaporeans to do our part to uphold higher standards of hygiene and cleanliness.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Last year, the PHC organised a workshop with residents and other community partners to brainstorm anti-littering interventions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: As a follow-up to realise one of the ideas PHC partnered with Nanyang Polytechnic to develop a Smart Bin prototype, which was subsequently tested within the neighbourhood and now will be scaled up.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NEA is also working together with residents of 21 private estates, such as Jalan Wajek in Bukit Timah, in an interesting initiative.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Residents park their vehicles on just one side of the road on specified days to facilitate mechanical road sweepers cleaning the other side of the road.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This achieved 50% to 80% of time savings compared to manual labour.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NEA will like to double the number of private estates involved in this initiative.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We look forward to more of such support from residents as we transition to using cleaning technology.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To reduce the public’s exposure to second-hand smoke, we currently prohibit smoking at more than 49,000 premises.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Last month, NEA adjusted the Orchard Road No-Smoking Zone (ORNSZ) to include additional areas where smokers congregate.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To Mr Louis Ng’s question, NEA will continue to monitor the situation and consult relevant stakeholders, before considering extension of non-smoking areas.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To Mr Gan’s query, indeed, as smoking is prohibited at all covered areas, including buildings and retail food establishments, smokers may congregate in adjacent spaces where smoking is not prohibited.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Stakeholders interested in setting up designated smoking points (DSPs) can refer to guidelines on NEA’s website and seek NEA's advice, if needed.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: These should be at least five metres away from the premises boundary and direct smokers away from the general public.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The proliferation of DSPs needs to be carefully considered and balanced against the risk of inadvertently normalising smoking.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Ng also asked about second-hand smoke within homes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In addition to working with other Government agencies and the community to issue joint advisories, we will continue to encourage smokers to practise greater social responsibility and facilitate conversations between neighbours.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Based on NEA’s data from 2018 to 2022, about 95% of feedback providers did not give further feedback on smoking in homes within a year after advisories were issued.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We remain open to innovative and practical solutions to reduce public exposure to second-hand smoke.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Chairman, I will now continue my speech in Mandarin.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: (In Mandarin):   As announced by Minister Fu, MSE has designated this year to be the Year of Public Hygiene.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This signifies the importance of safeguarding public health and providing a green and thriving home for all.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I will speak more about our efforts to maintain a clean environment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: During our ForwardSG engagements, Singaporeans acknowledged that keeping Singapore clean and green is a whole-of-society effort, and that we cannot rely only on cleaners and cleaning technology.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: As part of our multi-pronged approach to keep the environment clean, we will intensify our efforts in managing hotspots.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will conduct larger-scale blitzes at hotspots more frequently.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: If we are unable to identify the offenders, we will work with community stakeholders to publicise the images of offenders at the neighbourhoods where they littered to get information of these offenders from members of the public. : Mr Chairman, public engagement is also one of the main levers to shape social norms and individual behaviours.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Hence, MSE launched the inaugural Go Green SG campaign in 2023.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: There was a diverse slate of activities, including behind-the-scenes tours, workshops and other community events to help participants develop a deeper appreciation of Singapore’s sustainability efforts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Go Green SG will return this year, with a focus on public hygiene, with an expanded range of activities, to welcome more participants to build a cleaner and greener Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Our youths are deeply passionate about the environment and sustainability.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: It is essential to provide them with a better understanding of the relevant issues so that they can contribute meaningfully to national policy discussions and efforts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Hence, the Government has several initiatives to strengthen our partnership with the youth community by raising awareness on climate issues and galvanising action among our youths.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: They had a fireside chat with Minister Fu and gained a deeper understanding of Singapore’s climate and sustainability considerations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Last year, they also participated in platforms, such as the Earthshot Prize Awards, Singapore International Energy Week and COP28.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This allowed youths to engage climate change negotiators, policymakers, businesses and non-profit organisations, and develop a more nuanced understanding of climate and sustainability issues.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To continue growing this community of young environmental advocates, we will be co-creating the second run together with participants from the inaugural cohort.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Senior Parliamentary Secretary Baey, I hope you are finishing your speech.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, we are heartened by the enthusiasm and contributions by our youths to shape a more sustainable future.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The Government does not have a monopoly over the best ideas.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: To better navigate the changing environment and social context, MSE will continue to enable and empower Singaporeans to be stewards of a clean, green and sustainable future.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Minister Fu, you have a clarification to make.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Mr Chairman, may I have your permission to make a correction, please?

speaker: The Chairman
text: So, Members, those who want to raise clarifications, keep it short.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Sorry, Mr Chairman, I do have a correction to make for my speech.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In my speech, I said that the median rental across non-subsidised hawker stalls remains at $1,225.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I think he mentioned 95% of the feedback providers do not get back to us.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I think one of the reasons they do not get back is because they realise there is not much we can do other than issue advisories.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: So, could I ask again that the Ministry study what else we can do other than just issuing advisories?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Second, maybe we could set up a taskforce, like the Public Toilet Taskforce.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: We could set up one taskforce to study this issue of second-hand smoke as well.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: As discussed, many times in this Chamber, there are practical challenges on legislating against smoking at homes.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The cost involved in enforcing and the practicality of being able to enforcing such acts within the private spaces of homes is a big challenge that we have not had the solution yet.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Yes, I do encourage, if residents are still bothered by second-hand smoke, to continue giving feedback because based on data, indeed, 95% did not come back to us.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: I am not sure whether is it that all of them do not think that it is useful to continue giving us feedback.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: With data, we are better usable to assess and for us to see how else we can work on addressing this issue.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, I beg the Member's patience and understanding.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: One is to Senior Minister of State Amy Khor in relation to the climate-friendly vouchers.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I understand that she has shared some figures.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The second clarification is to Senior Parliamentary Secretary Baey, in relation to the Public Toilet Taskforce.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I wonder how does that differ from the past campaigns and collaborations, for example, that NEA already had with Public Hygiene Councils?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: What is the key takeaway from the past collaborations that we really want to implement from this new public toilet taskforce?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: First, I think households are more likely to utilise the vouchers if they need to replace their old or faulty fittings and appliances.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And, of course, many of these appliances would last a few years.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Under the current CFHB, the vouchers are limited to three different types of products.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, I think that does not allow a lot of flexibility.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Although, when we sized it, it was based on how we can offset some of the differential upfront costs and the higher upfront costs for the more energy-efficient types, and these are the essential household appliances and fittings.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: They can use different denominations to purchase these products.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We hope that with the expansion in scope in terms of coverage of products as well as households and with, more flexibility, we hope that utilisation rate will be higher.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We are working with HDB, People's Association as well as with grassroots organisations and the retailers to reach out and raise awareness.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: For past campaigns over the years, we look at general cleanliness of public toilets.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: And I would say that there have been improvements.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, we will take a more targeted focus on these premises, and we will also have a better understanding with the involvement of the coffee shop associations to understand the challenges of coffee shop operators in maintaining the public toilets.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Is it a matter of resources or is it the design of the toilet?

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, we will look at all these aspects and, hopefully, we will be able to come up with some recommendations and solutions to make our public toilets in coffee shops and hawker centres cleaner.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: Specifically, my clarification is whether MSE will consider setting some proactive goals to convert Singaporeans to alternative ways of treating the remains, such as inland ash scattering, instead of waiting for the numbers to grow organically?

speaker: The Chairman
text: If not, could I invite Mr Louis Ng to indicate if you would like to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: And I thank Minister Grace Fu, Senior Minister of State Koh Poh Koon, Senior Minister of State Amy Khor and Senior Parliamentary Secretary Baey Yam Keng for their commitment and leadership towards our economic resilience, resource resilience and climate resilience.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: But we cannot be resilient towards second-hand smoke, so I hope we are equally committed towards tackling this problem.
